body:

Client follow-up templates for your next conversation.

Find your follow-up Mix.

Useful wording for the conversations independent professionals actually need to continue: an estimate that’s out, a proposal under review, a client who said “not yet”. Every example here is original and illustrative, not a customer quote. Make the wording yours, then try the matching follow-up plan in the demo.

Templates by situation
Estimate follow-up text templates

Three texts and one email for an estimate that’s out for a decision: the check-in you promised, the customer who needed time, and timing that may have changed.

Contractors and trades

Proposal follow-up email templates

Emails for a proposal under review: the agreed review date, an unclear decision process, and a timeline that moved.

Consultants and professional services

More situations are added as their examples are reviewed. Nothing is published as a placeholder.

Follow-up plans by profession

Each page plays a demo with that profession’s own Mixes, so you can see the plan before you read the template.

Real Estate Agents: Make “not yet” a plan to check back.
Consultants: Give proposals a next step while you deliver current work.

Follow-up reminders for the things you said you’d do.

A little rhythm. A lot less remembering.

A follow-up reminder in Jump in the Mix is a Beat: one scheduled message or call step inside a Mix, your reusable follow-up plan. Here is who gets reminded, what shows up when it’s due, and which parts stay with you.

Who gets the reminder

You do. Reminders go to you, never to your contacts. Each Beat is a note to yourself that a planned check-in is due, with the draft you prepared for it.

What appears when a Beat is due

Your Today list shows the Beats due today, anything overdue, and what’s coming this week. The next one is marked “Next up”, with the message ready to open in your own text or email app, or the call notes ready for a phone call. Editing the draft happens right there, before anything is sent.

Optional notifications, off until you turn them on
A daily email. A digest of the day’s follow-ups, sent at the hour you choose in your saved timezone.
A push notification when Beats become due. Items due together are grouped, quiet hours are respected, and a reminder arrives after the next background check, so it can take a few minutes. On iPhone or iPad, add the site to your Home Screen first.
A weekly summary email. A look at the week ahead, each Monday.

Turn any of them on in Settings under Notifications. Nothing is sent to you until you do.

What stays with you
Sending. A Beat opens your own messaging or email app with the draft ready, or you copy it into whichever app you prefer. Nothing goes out on its own unless you connect an optional sending provider and turn that on.
Recording what happened. Mark a Beat sent, not sent, no answer, left a voicemail, rescheduled, or skipped. A reminder is never treated as proof that a message was sent.
Deciding the next step. Jump in the Mix doesn’t read replies. If someone answers, declines, or asks you to stop, you change the plan.

In the demo, open a planned Beat and choose its date. In the product, that date is when the Beat lands on your Today list.

Your information and privacy

Effective 2026-09-09

Jump in the Mix operates Jump in the Mix. Contact support@jumpinthemix.com about your account, privacy, or information someone else has entered about you.

What you provide

We store your account details and the contacts, notes, dates, mixes, follow-up history, and preferences you save. Joining the waitlist records your email and confirmation or access status without creating a customer account. If you join from a profession example, we can retain that allowlisted example choice through your invitation so the matching starter is ready to review; we do not retain your sandbox message edits or fictional contact. Invitations record the sender, recipient, and access and delivery history. Support conversations contain the information you choose to share.

Only add information you have permission to use. Avoid adding unnecessary sensitive information to contact notes or support messages.

How we use information

We use these records to operate your account, prepare your follow-up list, provide connections and notifications you enable, deliver requested account, invitation, and support emails, answer support requests, and protect the service. Operational records support sending limits, recipient opt-outs, delivery recovery, security, and reliability.

Messages and service providers

By default, you review a follow-up and send it through your chosen messaging app. Automatic sending requires a configured provider and your opt-in. Personal invitation links are prepared as reminders in Today. You review and send them through your own text or email app.

The production service uses Render for hosting and database storage, Resend for application email, and Amazon Web Services for independently stored encrypted backups and recovery keys.
